verdict_text:
YES

The script uses `scale = lora_alpha / r = 2`, computes `B @ A` in float32 without transposition (correct for `fan_in_fan_out = false`), adds to the float32-upcast base and casts back to float16, leaving names/shapes/dtypes intact and every other tensor untouched. All four required checks are asserted before writing, and the sharding packs in order with a 536,870,912-byte cap, flushing before any tensor that would exceed it so an oversized tensor lands alone, with a `weight_map` covering all 244 names.
